pointers.sentence: Its subclasses are the `<input>` widgets, among them the file inputs and `CheckboxInput`, `Textarea`, the choice widgets, and the widgets of several inputs, `MultiWidget`, `SplitDateTimeWidget` and `SelectDateWidget` (`django/forms/widgets.py`).
`Widget.__init__` keeps a copy of the HTML attributes it is given as `Widget.attrs`; the rest is flags, class attributes that other objects read (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget`).

A field sets `Widget.is_required` on its widget, and `Widget.is_localized` if it is localized, and merges its `Field.widget_attrs` into the attributes, as a `CharField` adds `"maxlength"` ([A form field: the base class](fields.md)) (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.__init__`).

A hidden field is drawn among the form's hidden fields, and its input gets neither `"required"` nor `"aria-invalid"` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.is_hidden`, `django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).

A hidden field is drawn among the form's hidden fields, and its input gets neither `"required"` nor `"aria-invalid"` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.is_hidden`, `django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).

`Widget.render` asks `Widget.get_context` for a dictionary and hands it to `Widget._render`, which has the renderer it was given, or the default one, render the widget's template with it, and marks the result safe (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.render`, `django/forms/widgets.py:Widget._render`).

`Widget.render` asks `Widget.get_context` for a dictionary and hands it to `Widget._render`, which has the renderer it was given, or the default one, render the widget's template with it, and marks the result safe (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.render`, `django/forms/widgets.py:Widget._render`).
In a form the caller is `BoundField.as_widget`, with the form's renderer and attributes such as `"id"` and `"required"` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).

The context's one key, `"widget"`, holds the name, `"is_hidden"`, `"required"`, the value as `Widget.format_value` writes it, `"template_name"`, and the attributes: the widget's own and then the call's, which win, merged by `Widget.build_attrs` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.get_context`).

`Widget.format_value` turns an empty string, `None`, and the `DatabaseDefault` an unsaved instance holds for a database default into `None`, for which the template writes no `"value"`; a localized widget formats the value with `django.utils.formats.localize_input`, which leaves a string as it is; any other value becomes `str(value)` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.format_value`).

The attributes are written by `"django/forms/widgets/attrs.html"`, which leaves out one that is `False` and writes one that is `True` bare (`django/forms/templates/django/forms/widgets/attrs.html`); where the templates are found is in [Rendering a form: renderers and templates](rendering.md).

`Widget.value_from_datadict` is given the form's data, its files and the input's name, and returns the raw value that `Field.clean` starts from when the field is not disabled: in the base class, what the data holds under that name, or `None` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.value_from_datadict`).

The form asks the widget and not the field because, as the comment in `BaseForm._widget_data_value` says, some widgets split their data over several HTML inputs (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm._widget_data_value`).

Besides the widgets made of others, its reader is `construct_instance`, which leaves a model field that has a default as the instance holds it when the widget says its input was omitted and the cleaned value is empty ([Model forms: `ModelForm` and `fields_for_model`](model-forms.md)) (`django/forms/models.py:construct_instance`).

`Widget.id_for_label` gives the id a `<label>` names in its `"for"`: in the base class the input's own; for a widget of several inputs, one of theirs, or an empty string, which leaves the label without a `"for"` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.id_for_label`).
The bound field writes `"required"` only when the widget agrees, the field is required and `BaseForm.use_required_attribute` is true (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).
Its `Input.input_type`, which its subclasses set, goes into the context as `"type"`, and a `"type"` among the attributes an instance is made with replaces it (`django/forms/widgets.py:Input`).
`PasswordInput` draws no value unless made with `render_value=True`, so a form sent back with errors does not repeat the password (`django/forms/widgets.py:PasswordInput.get_context`).
`MultipleHiddenInput` draws a hidden input for each value of a list and reads the list back with `getlist` (`django/forms/widgets.py:MultipleHiddenInput`).
`Textarea`, which is no `Input`, writes the value between its tags, with `"cols"` of `"40"` and `"rows"` of `"10"` unless given others (`django/forms/widgets.py:Textarea.__init__`).

The date and time inputs share `DateTimeBaseInput`, which writes a value in its `DateTimeBaseInput.format`, if it was made with one, or else in the first of the locale's formats named by `DateTimeBaseInput.format_key`, as `DATE_INPUT_FORMATS`; a string it leaves alone ([Locale formats: `get_format` and the format modules](../i18n/formats.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:DateTimeBaseInput.format_value`).

`FileInput` reads from the files and not the data, counts as omitted when its name is not among them, never draws a value, and refuses `"required"` when the field has an initial value (`django/forms/widgets.py:FileInput`).

Given one, the template writes a link to it and, for a field that is not required, a checkbox named after the input with `"-clear"` added, as `"scan-clear"`, before the file input (`django/forms/templates/django/forms/widgets/clearable_file_input.html`).

Ticked with no upload, it returns `False`, which `FileField.clean` takes as an order to clear the stored file; ticked with an upload too, the marker `FILE_INPUT_CONTRADICTION`, which the field makes an error ([The built-in form fields](field-types.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:ClearableFileInput.value_from_datadict`, `django/forms/fields.py:FileField.clean`).

Ticked with no upload, it returns `False`, which `FileField.clean` takes as an order to clear the stored file; ticked with an upload too, the marker `FILE_INPUT_CONTRADICTION`, which the field makes an error ([The built-in form fields](field-types.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:ClearableFileInput.value_from_datadict`, `django/forms/fields.py:FileField.clean`).

By default that is `boolean_check`, true of anything but `False`, `None` and the empty string, a function at module level so that the widget can be pickled, as the comment above it says, citing ticket 17976 (`django/forms/widgets.py:boolean_check`).

Otherwise it reads `"true"` and `"false"`, in any case, as `True` and `False`, and anything else by its truth, so that `"0"` is `True`, and so is `"on"`: by HTML's rule a browser sends that for a ticked box with no `"value"`, and `CheckboxInput.format_value` writes none for `True` (`django/forms/widgets.py:CheckboxInput.value_from_datadict`).
What `BooleanField` makes of the value is in [The built-in form fields](field-types.md) (`django/forms/fields.py:BooleanField`).
`MultiWidget` draws one field as several inputs and reads it back as a list (`django/forms/widgets.py:MultiWidget`).

To draw, it hands a value that is not a list or a tuple to `MultiWidget.decompress`, which subclasses write, and has each widget make its context with its own name, value and id (`django/forms/widgets.py:MultiWidget.get_context`).

`SplitDateTimeWidget` is a `MultiWidget` of a `DateInput` and a `TimeInput`; its `SplitDateTimeWidget.decompress` splits a datetime, an aware one first made naive in the current time zone (`django/forms/widgets.py:SplitDateTimeWidget.decompress`).

`SelectDateWidget` draws a date as three `<select>` boxes, named after the field with `"_year"`, `"_month"` and `"_day"` added, in the order of the locale's `DATE_FORMAT`; it is no `MultiWidget`, and makes a `Select` for each box itself (`django/forms/widgets.py:SelectDateWidget`).
